'''Stanley Stephen Shillington''' (January 21, 1935 – December 8, 2025) was a Canadian lacrosse historian, sportswriter and statistician.<ref name="obit">{{cite web|title=Statistician was vital in preserving history of Canada's official summer sport|last=Hawthorn|first=Tom|date=December 24, 2025|publisher=The Globe and Mail|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-statistician-was-vital-in-preserving-history-of-canadas-official/|access-date=January 29, 2026}}</ref> Throughout his career, Shillington was the scorekeeper for a total of 971 games, including regular season, playoffs, and [[Mann Cup]] games. He was inducted into the [[Canadian Lacrosse Hall of Fame]] as a builder in 1977.

==Career==
As a kid growing up in Vancouver, Shillington saw his first senior lacrosse game during the 1946–47 season.<ref name = ":1">{{cite web |last1=Gombar |first1=Jeff |title=Lacrosse Historian Passes Torch |url=https://www.bclacrosse.com/pdfs/lacrossetalk/lacrossetalk-2015-spring.pdf |website=bclacrosse.com |accessdate=August 24, 2019 |page=19 |date=Spring 2015}}</ref> He began playing junior lacrosse under the direction of Reginald "Pop" Phillips.<ref>{{cite web |title=British Columbia Lacrosse Association Down Memory Lane |url=https://bclaregistration.com/general/memory-lane/phillips-reginald.cfm |website=bclaregistration.com |accessdate=August 27, 2019}}</ref> Although he enjoyed playing lacrosse, Shillington was forced to quit to take a job as a night copy boy at the [[Vancouver Sun]]. To increase his income, he also wrote one-paragraph game reports on minor and junior lacrosse games, then started adding league stats every couple of weeks.<ref name = "wlalacrosse">{{cite web |title=A Passion For Numbers, Lacrosse |url=http://wlalacrosse.com/view/wla/lifetime-stats |website=wlalacrosse.com |accessdate=August 24, 2019}}</ref>

Shillington then accepted a job as the newspapers police reporter and researcher with the Joint Coordinated Law Enforcement Unit. Despite this, he still kept a log of statistics on lacrosse games as a hobby.<ref name = "wlalacrosse"/> Shillington later recounted the 1951 Mann Cup between the [[Peterborough Timbermen]] and [[Vancouver Combines]], dubbing it the Mann Cup Follies for the league's "continually flip-flopped in its decision-making" and intolerable conditions the players played in.<ref>{{cite news |title=Remembering the Mann Cup Follies faced by the Timbermen |url=https://www.thepeterboroughexaminer.com/sports-story/8221703-remembering-the-mann-cup-follies-faced-by-the-timbermen/ |accessdate=August 27, 2019 |agency=The Peterborough Examiner |date=June 3, 2016}}</ref>

In 1953, Shillington became one of the founders of the Renfrew Athletic Club and later the Fraser Lacrosse Commission.<ref name = ":1"/> While working as Secretary of the Renfrew Athletic Club in 1954, he was contacted by Art Daoust, head of the Lacrosse Junior league, to record stats for the league and write the occasional story. After proving to be successful at this task, Shillington was contacted by Tom Gordon, head of  Inter City Lacrosse League (ICLL), in 1957, to be the ICLL statistician. His position with the ICLL began with the Vancouver Minor Association in 1955–1960. In total, he spent 31 seasons as league statistician with the ICLL and [[Western Lacrosse Association]] (WLA).<ref name = ":1"/> Shillington would later be named the Official Canadian Lacrosse Association Mann Cup Statistician.<ref name = "CSHOF">{{cite web |title=Shillington Called to CSHOF |url=https://www.clhof.org/images/LacrosseTalk/Papers/Fall%202011%20Issue.pdf |website=clhof.org |accessdate=August 25, 2019 |date=Fall 2011}}</ref> Shillington recounted having to once score a game from the penalty box while two players attacked each other with sticks over his head.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hawthorn |first1=Tom |title=Gritty amateur players aren't alone in reaching for cloud nine |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/gritty-amateur-players-arent-alone-in-reaching-for-cloud-nine/article18430362/ |accessdate=August 25, 2019 |publisher=The Globe and Mail |date=September 9, 2003}}</ref> In 1970, he was awarded the Art Daoust Merit Award. In 1977 he was inducted into the [[Canadian Lacrosse Hall of Fame]] as a builder.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stan Shillington (Supplemental) |url=https://www.clhof.org/index.php/inductees/inductee-supplemental-pages/1281-stan-shillington-supplemental |website=clhof.org |accessdate=August 25, 2019}}</ref> In 1980, Shillington awarded the Norm Kowalyk Trophy as Executive Of The Year by the Western Lacrosse Association.<ref name = "esportsdesk">{{cite web |title=WLA Records (1943 - 2012) |url=http://www.esportsdesk.com/media/leagues/5357/graphics/WLA%202012%20Media%20Guide%20WLA%20AWARDS%20&%20RECORDS.pdf |website=esportsdesk.com |accessdate=August 25, 2019}}</ref> That same year, he published ''Who's Who In Lacrosse.''<ref>{{cite web |title=Lacrosse Research |url=http://www.wampsbibleoflacrosse.com/newstats/Chapter-14.pdf |website=wampsbibleoflacrosse.com |accessdate=August 27, 2019 |page=10}}</ref>

Due to his statistical background, Shillington was asked to help two Ontario historians in 2002 research lost statistical information from Ontario Senior “A” lacrosse games that were never recorded or compiled.<ref name = "CSHOF"/> Beginning in 2008, the Western Lacrosse Association's CKNW "TOP DOG" Trophy for the Winners of League Play was replaced by the Stan Shillington Trophy.<ref name = "esportsdesk"/>

In 2011, Shillington was inducted in the second induction class of the [[Canada's Sports Hall of Fame]].<ref name = "CSHOF"/> He was also inducted into the Coquitlam Sports Hall of Fame.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hall of Fame—2011 Inductees |url=https://www.coquitlamshof.com/halloffameinductees2011.cfm |website=coquitlamshof.com |accessdate=August 25, 2019}}</ref> In 2019, Doug Luey, [[Major Series Lacrosse]] commissioner and president of the Jr. B Green Gaels said, “If it wasn’t for him [Larry Power] and his efforts and Stan Shillington in B.C., there would be no lacrosse records.”<ref>{{cite web |last1=McNair |first1=Brian |title=Bible of lacrosse lasting legacy of Larry 'Wamper' Power |url=https://www.durhamregion.com/community-story/9456338-bible-of-lacrosse-lasting-legacy-of-larry-wamper-power/ |website=durhamregion.com |accessdate=August 25, 2019 |date=June 27, 2019}}</ref> He died of complications of dementia on December 8, 2025, in Burnaby, British Columbia.<ref name="obit" />
